transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning and thank you for calling S-Net Digital Home Support. My name is Kieran. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Kieran, my name is Niamh. I'm calling from my 83-year-old mother Brigid's house because her landline was switched over to S-Net Digital Voice yesterday and now her fall-alarm pendant unit won't connect.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: To make matters worse, whenever anyone rings the house phone, the screen just says 'Unknown Caller' instead of showing our family numbers, so she's frightened to pick up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am so sorry for the worry this has caused both you and your mother, Niamh. When an elderly parent relies on a telecare fall pendant and caller display for safety, having both fail after a switchover is deeply concerning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am going to take personal charge of getting both her telecare pendant alarm and her incoming caller ID working properly during this call. First, may I verify the installation address and the four-digit security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, Kieran. I'm listed as the authorised power-of-attorney contact on her account. The address is 28 St. Finbarr's Gardens, Bristol, BS9 3QT, and the security PIN is 4815.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Niamh—I can see you registered as the primary authorised representative alongside your mother Brigid, and both the address and PIN are verified.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me make sure I have captured everything accurately: since yesterday's Digital Voice migration onto the router's phone port, your mother's telecare pendant alarm base unit fails to connect to its monitoring centre, and incoming calls no longer display caller ID on her handset.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's exactly it. The engineer left a green adapter cable plugged into the back of the S-Net Hub, and we get a dial tone on the phone, but when we ran our monthly pendant test this morning, the alarm unit beeped with a line fault.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for explaining that so clearly, Niamh. Let's walk through a few diagnostic questions about the physical equipment so I can see how the signals are travelling.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Of course, I'm standing right next to the hallway table where the router and the alarm box sit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you tell me the make and model printed on your mother's telecare base unit, and what colour light is currently showing on the front of that unit?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's a Tunstall Lifeline Vi+ unit provided by the local council telecare team. Normally the status ring is steady green, but after the failed test call twenty minutes ago it's flashing red and amber.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I know the Tunstall Lifeline Vi+ very well, Niamh. How are the Tunstall unit and your mother's cordless telephone connected into the green TEL1 port on the back of the S-Net Hub?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is a short green RJ11-to-BT adapter plugged into the TEL1 socket on the back of the S-Net Hub. The Tunstall box is plugged into that adapter, and then Mum's Panasonic cordless base station plugs into the back of the Tunstall box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That physical daisy-chain order—Hub TEL1 to Tunstall first, then the Panasonic handset plugged into the Tunstall's pass-through socket—is actually the exact right wiring order for priority line seizure.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, good! I was worried we had plugged the two leads in the wrong way round when we tidied the cables yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, you wired that part spot on, Niamh. Now, when you pressed the red pendant button earlier today, what exactly did you hear from the Tunstall speaker before it gave the fault beep?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It gave the usual reassurance announcement saying 'Calling for help, please wait', then I heard it dial out, the monitoring centre seemed to pick up, and then there were lots of rapid high-pitched beeps that kept failing until it hung up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Those rapid high-pitched beeps are the critical clue I needed, Niamh! The Tunstall Lifeline Vi+ uses analogue in-band DTMF handshake tones—specifically the BS 8521 / CPC protocol—to transmit your mother's client ID to the receiving centre.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so why did those tones stop working when we moved from the old copper wall socket to the router port?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When Digital Voice provisions with a standard residential profile, the voice port sometimes compresses audio and intercepts DTMF tones digitally, which clips the fast acoustic handshake tones that a Tunstall telecare unit expects.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, I see! Is that something you can change on the line from your side, or does our council telecare technician have to replace the box?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can fix that directly from here by switching your mother's Digital Voice port to our uncompressed G.711 pass-through profile with analogue tone relay enabled.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What a relief! And what about the caller ID showing 'Unknown' on her Panasonic cordless screen? She won't answer the phone unless she can see it's me or my sister calling.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the SIP voice profile on the exchange switch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I can see the port setting is currently forcing compressed audio and ETS ETSI FSK caller ID instead of UK SIN 227 Bellcore polarity-reversal caller ID.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, so her UK Panasonic handset doesn't understand the European caller ID signal that the router is sending out?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Precisely, Niamh. Older and standard UK cordless handsets like your mother's Panasonic expect a brief line-polarity reversal pulse before the first ring to wake up the caller display chip.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why the screen lights up on the first ring but just says 'Unknown Caller' every single time!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also, while looking at your mother's account flags, I noticed that the Priority Services Register telecare marker was not ticked when the migration order completed yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Really? I definitely told the sales advisor last month that Mum wears a council fall-detection pendant and is eighty-three.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am very glad I spotted that today, Niamh. While our specialist vulnerable-customer engineering desk normally audits post-migration telecare accounts within seventy-two hours, I am taking complete ownership of everything myself right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much, Kieran. Does adding that Priority Services marker also mean she gets a battery backup unit in case there is a power cut in Bristol?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it does! As part of adding the Priority Services medical-pendant flag today, I am also raising a complimentary UPS battery backup unit dispatch through our specialist vulnerable-customer engineering desk so her Hub and Tunstall line stay powered during an outage.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is wonderful—that was actually the next thing on my list to ask about because winter storms sometimes trip the village power for an hour.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will have that battery backup order reference confirmed for you before we finish. First, let's get her live line fixed right now so we can test both the Tunstall pendant and the Panasonic caller ID together.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, let's do that first while I'm here at her house.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To apply the uncompressed G.711 telecare profile, enable in-band BS 8521 tone pass-through, and switch Caller Display to UK SIN 227 polarity pulse, I need to rebuild the voice port on her Hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will that cut off our call right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are you calling me from your mobile phone today, Niamh, or from the house landline?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, good point—I'm calling you from my mobile because I knew we'd be testing the landline!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That makes things much easier! The green Voice LED on the S-Net Hub will go out for about a minute while the TEL1 port resets. Please bear with me while I rebuild the analogue adapter bridge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No problem at all, Kieran, take all the time you need.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you so much for holding, Niamh, I have rebuilt the voice profile and re-provisioned the TEL1 port with the telecare G.711 codec and UK SIN 227 caller display enabled.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I was watching the router while you were doing that—the green phone symbol blinked for about thirty seconds and it has just turned solid green again!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And has the flashing red-and-amber fault warning on the Tunstall Lifeline Vi+ base unit changed now that the line voltage has stabilised?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look closely at the Tunstall box... Yes! The warning beep stopped and the ring around the main button is back to a steady solid green!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That means the Tunstall unit has detected steady line voltage again. First, let's test the incoming caller ID on your mother's Panasonic cordless handset before we run the live pendant alarm test.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'm holding the Panasonic handset right here in my hand.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am going to trigger an automated test ring to your mother's landline from our S-Net diagnostic number ending in 0800 right now. Tell me what appears on the handset screen when it rings.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's ringing now... and look at the screen! It shows the full 0800 number and 'S-Net Test' right above it! Mum, look, the numbers are back on the screen!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is lovely to hear, Niamh! I've ended the test ring now. If you also want to verify with a family number later, any contacts stored in the Panasonic phonebook will match up and display their names again too.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will give her so much peace of mind. Now, can we stay on the line while I press the red button on her Tunstall pendant to make sure the monitoring centre actually receives the digital handshake?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Absolutely—I would not end this call without verifying the live telecare alarm test with you. When the monitoring operator answers over the Tunstall speakerphone, just let them know it is a post-Digital-Voice line test.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I'm pressing the red button on Mum's pendant now... The Tunstall base unit has lit up red and announced 'Calling for help, please wait'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see the outbound call active on the TEL1 SIP channel in uncompressed G.711 mode. Let's listen for the handshake tones.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's dialling... the monitoring centre just answered, I just heard two clean bursts of tones instead of the endless beeping... and a lady on the speakerphone just said 'Good morning Mrs O'Connor, we have received your test call clearly!'

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Two clean bursts and an immediate operator greeting—that means the BS 8521 DTMF telemetry packet went through on the very first attempt with zero packet loss.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've just thanked the telecare operator and she cleared the call down from her desk, and the Tunstall Lifeline Vi+ has gone straight back to a steady green ring!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can confirm from the call trace here that the monitoring centre sent the clear-down tone cleanly and the port released back to idle with zero errors.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Kieran, I cannot thank you enough. My mum was sitting in the armchair looking so anxious all morning, and she's smiling again now that she heard the telecare lady on the speaker.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please pass on my warmest wishes to Brigid, Niamh—nobody should ever be left feeling unsafe in their own home after a phone line upgrade.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I certainly will. And did the order for the battery backup unit go through okay as well?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I have locked the Priority Services Register medical-telecare flag onto her account permanently, and the complimentary S-Net Extended Battery Backup unit is booked under order reference BBU-90412 for courier delivery tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tomorrow! That is fantastic service. Does the battery backup unit just plug in between the power socket and the router?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, and because your mother is on the Priority Services Register, our field technician will actually install the battery backup unit for her tomorrow afternoon between two and four o'clock at no charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Even better, I'll be here at the house tomorrow afternoon anyway so I can let the technician in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we wrap up today, Niamh, let's do a final check: incoming caller ID is displaying numbers on the Panasonic handset, and the Tunstall Lifeline Vi+ pendant test succeeded live with the monitoring centre—is everything with the landline resolved to your satisfaction?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Kieran, just one quick question before we finish—if there is ever a broadband maintenance update overnight, will that reset the G.711 telecare setting you just built?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is a very sensible question, Niamh. Because I bound the telecare G.711 profile to the master exchange service template rather than a temporary router override, any overnight firmware update will automatically pull down the exact same telecare settings.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that's brilliant, so we don't have to worry about it reverting back to the compressed profile if the Hub reboots?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all—even if the S-Net Hub is switched off at the wall or receives a firmware upgrade, it will always boot up with UK SIN 227 caller ID and uncompressed BS 8521 telecare tone pass-through active.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And should we still run our usual monthly test on the red pendant button just to be good practice?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the telecare monitoring centre always recommends a quick monthly press of the pendant, and when our technician installs the battery backup unit tomorrow afternoon, they will also test the failover on battery power with you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives both me and my sister complete confidence leaving Mum here this evening. Thank you again for being so thorough.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are more than welcome, Niamh. Everything we discussed—the voice port profile, the Priority Services marker, and tomorrow's BBU-90412 installation—is fully documented in the account notes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, one hundred percent resolved. Both the telecare alarm and the caller ID are working perfectly, and the battery backup is sorted too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been an absolute pleasure helping you and your mother today, Niamh. If you ever need anything else, we are here twenty-four seven. Thank you for choosing S-Net, and have a lovely rest of your day.
